newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN WINS AUSTRIAN GRAND PRIX.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN WINS AUSTRIAN GRAND PRIX.

text.p: Three-times 500cc world champion Michael Doohan extended his lead in the standings by recording his fourth victory of the season at the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday.
The Australian Honda rider, who now has 38 career wins, finished 22.077 seconds ahead of Japanese team mate Tadayuki Okada and 22.471 in front of Italian Luca Cadalora on a Yamaha.
Okada, who was an uncertain starter after he sustained an injury to his left hip in Saturday's final qualifying, capitalised on an error by Spanish team mate Alex Criville on the penultimate lap.
Criville, who now trails Doohan in the standings by 31 points, was second for most of the 28-lap race but went off the track after a mistake and finished fifth.
Olivier Jacque of France won the 250cc race after overtaking Germany's Ralf Waldmann on the final lap. World champion Max Biaggi of Italy extended his lead in the standings with third place.
Japanese Honda rider Noburu Ueda took the lead in the 125cc standings from Aprilia's Valentino Rossi -- winning in 40:19.719, just 0.004 seconds ahead of the Italian.
